name: Supermarket Near Me in Singapore: Best Ways to Find Groceries and Food Shopping
content:
When you search "supermarket near me," you're usually trying to solve an immediate need — restocking the fridge, finding a specific brand, or figuring out where to shop after moving to a new area. In Singapore, most residents have several supermarket options within a short walk or bus ride, but the right choice depends on what you're buying, your budget, and how much time you have.

This guide explains how to actually find the nearest supermarket using tools that know your location, what to expect from Singapore's main supermarket chains, and how to shop more efficiently across both physical stores and online options.

Key takeaways

  • Your phone's Google Maps or Apple Maps app — using live GPS — is the most reliable way to find a supermarket near me, since this website cannot detect your physical location.
  • Singapore's major supermarket chains are NTUC FairPrice, Sheng Siong, Giant, and Cold Storage, each with a different footprint, pricing pattern, and store format.
  • Sheng Siong has grown to over 70 stores islandwide and is especially strong in HDB heartland estates, while Giant has scaled back significantly, dropping to around 45 outlets in recent years.
  • Supermarket opening hours vary — some FairPrice and Sheng Siong outlets operate extended or 24-hour hours, while others follow standard mall or estate hours.
  • Combining a nearby supermarket visit with online grocery delivery gives you flexibility for both routine and last-minute shopping.

How to actually locate the nearest supermarket

Because this website can't access your live location, use one of these direct methods:

  1. Google Maps or Apple Maps — search "supermarket" with location services turned on; results are ranked by distance from where you're standing.
  2. Supermarket chain store locators — FairPrice, Sheng Siong, and Giant all maintain official store-locator pages listing every branch address, so you can confirm a store still exists at that location and check its operating hours.
  3. Grab, foodpanda, or Deliveroo apps — these show nearby supermarket partners for delivery, filtered automatically by your current location.
  4. Neighbourhood signage and town council directories — many HDB estates list nearby amenities, including supermarkets, on community noticeboards or town council websites.

Singapore's main supermarket chains compared

Chain Store count / presence Best known for
NTUC FairPrice Largest network in Singapore Widest coverage, competitive general pricing, FairPrice On for delivery
Sheng Siong Over 70 stores islandwide Value pricing, especially for fresh produce and meat; strong heartland presence
Giant Around 45 outlets (reduced footprint) Larger-format stores, often in malls; fewer locations than before
Cold Storage Moderate network, often in malls Slightly more premium range, imported and specialty items

Because Sheng Siong and FairPrice dominate the neighbourhood-level footprint, most residents searching "supermarket near me" in an HDB estate will find one of these two chains closest.

Which supermarket should you choose?

There's no single "cheapest" answer — it depends on your typical basket:

  • If you buy a lot of fresh produce and meat, Sheng Siong is frequently the more competitively priced option, based on independent price comparisons.
  • If you want the widest range and most locations, FairPrice's scale makes it the most convenient default, and its overall basket pricing has been found to be marginally lower in some comparisons.
  • If you're shopping for imported or specialty items, Cold Storage tends to carry a broader selection, usually at a higher price point.
  • If you're in a larger household and want to do a big monthly stock-up, a Giant outlet (where still available) or a hypermarket-format FairPrice may suit better due to bulk packaging options.

Supermarket opening hours: what to expect

Opening hours vary by outlet, not just by chain:

  • Some FairPrice and Sheng Siong branches operate 24 hours, particularly larger flagship stores.
  • Most neighbourhood branches run from roughly 7am to 11pm, though this varies by location.
  • Mall-based supermarkets (Cold Storage, some Giant outlets) generally follow mall opening hours, often 10am to 10pm.

Always check the specific outlet's listed hours via the chain's store locator before making a special trip, especially late at night or early morning.

Combining physical shopping with online options

If visiting a physical supermarket near you isn't practical, Singapore has well-established online grocery options:

  • FairPrice On — online ordering with delivery or self-collection
  • RedMart (via Lazada) — one of Singapore's longest-running online grocery platforms
  • Sheng Siong online store — delivery within their service coverage areas
  • Amazon Fresh Singapore — grocery delivery through Amazon's Singapore platform

Many residents use a hybrid approach: a physical supermarket run for fresh groceries and perishables, and online ordering for bulky household essentials that are heavier to carry home.

Frequently asked questions

How do I find the closest supermarket to where I am right now? Open Google Maps or Apple Maps, search "supermarket," and allow location access — the app will rank nearby options by distance using your device's live GPS.

Is Sheng Siong or FairPrice better value? It depends on what you're buying. Sheng Siong is often more competitive on fresh produce and meat, while FairPrice's overall basket price has sometimes come out slightly lower in comparison studies. Comparing prices on your usual items is the most reliable approach.

Are supermarkets open 24 hours in Singapore? Some are — certain FairPrice and Sheng Siong outlets operate 24 hours — but this varies by branch, so check the specific store's listed hours.

What if there isn't a supermarket close to my home? Check for minimarts or convenience stores for immediate needs, and consider online grocery delivery services like FairPrice On or RedMart for a fuller shop.

Has Giant reduced its number of stores? Yes. Giant's footprint in Singapore has shrunk in recent years, with the chain operating around 45 outlets, down from a larger network previously — check the official Giant store locator to confirm whether one is still near you.

Final practical takeaway

The fastest way to answer "supermarket near me" is to let your phone's GPS do the work through Google Maps or a chain's own store locator, since only your device knows your exact location. Once you've identified your nearby options, choose based on what you buy most — fresh produce shoppers often do better at Sheng Siong, while those wanting broad convenience tend to default to FairPrice.
